comment: Glyphs are CONTENT, like materials.json and reactions.json. A glyph is a word of the ancient language; docs/PLAN_magic_grammar.md is the grammar and scripts/magic_grammar.py the executable reference the C++ parser is checked against (`--gate spells-oracle`). Five sorts: matter (a material BY NAME, resolved to a 12-bit id at load; `air` is the void, `anything` the wildcard), effect (something that happens at a point: verb + params), delivery (how an effect reaches a point: mech instant | flight | continuous, plus the record fields), mod (a field edit on the delivery record: field/op/amount, applied again per repetition), operator (verb + valence: `left`/`right` list the sorts each slot accepts or `any`, `result` is the sort produced). Every unary operator takes the word BEFORE it; only an infix operator has both slots. Costs are integer: `word` is the small fixed cost of saying it; the real price is the tariff on what the cast does to the world (budgets.rates x the per-material `arcane` value in materials.json). Hot-reloads on R alongside materials.json. A delivery's `speed` is voxels per tick at 30 Hz and may be fractional (4.8 = 14.4 m/s); a flight collides with the CPU mirror, then the chunk cache it prefetches ahead of itself, then the ground contract, and with bodies by ray. A delivery's `look` block is RENDER-ONLY: shape bolt | ball | orb | spark, size (core half-size, voxels), tail (trailing sprites; the orb's ring count), tailStep (voxels between them), glow (emission), color (#RRGGBB, used when the cast carries no matter).
language: FOUR rules. R1 a noun goes into the PILE and order inside a scope of the pile does not matter: runs merge within a scope (fire fire = fire x2; matter and effects ADD, mods COMPOSE: shotgun x2 = 9) and the lowering rebuilds each scope in a canonical order. R2 a DELIVERY BOXES the innermost OPEN scope of the pile into one Effect value and speaking CONTINUES, so deliveries NEST and word order decides what is inside what; with no delivery the box is `hand`, at reach in front of the caster. R3 a MOD is pending and sticks to the box that closes the pile; on the hand only `shotgun`/`twin` (fanned resolve points) and `float`/`heavy` (the hop) mean anything and every other mod there is a charged no-op the readout names. R4 `lane` OPENS A LANE SCOPE and `end` CLOSES the innermost open one. A delivery inside an open lane boxes only that lane and the lane stays open; outside any lane it boxes the shared items plus every closed lane, which is the multi-socket box. Lanes are ordered as spoken, lane i belongs to instance i, the box fires max(count, lanes) instances, and an instance past the last lane carries the shared items alone. An unclosed lane is closed at the end of the sentence. Operators bind within the current scope only and a `lane`/`end` mark is a wall; a mod inside a lane edits that instance's record. A `count` mod SPLITS THE SCOPE it was spoken in - shared, it is the box's fan; inside a lane, it is that one branch's split - and at most ONE count word per scope is effective: the strongest wins, the rest are charged no-ops. Nine bolts is a split on each of three branches, not one word said twice. An operator with an empty required slot is INCOMPLETE: charged, does nothing, drawn with `_`; there are no defaults, `anything` and `air` are words. Every sequence lowers to a definite cast list; there is no misfire state.

budgets.comment: Rule 2 applied to magic: every sustained effect declares a FINITE budget up front. Hard engine ceilings; a glyph's own budget is clamped to them at load. rates.* and anythingSurchargeMille are the tariff (plan section 4): place = per voxel x arcane(M); convert = per voxel + max(0, arcane(B)-arcane(A)); graft = per voxel x arcane(M); explode = power x r^3 / 1000; wind = footprint x ticks / 1000. The wildcard bills value(actual) x surcharge on top, when it resolves.

hand.comment: The implicit delivery (R5). Not a glyph: it cannot be spoken, it is what a clause without a delivery is delivered by.
hand.desc: Implicit. At reach: a few voxels in front of the caster along the aim.

glyphs.desc: Nothing. The word for empty space. Sprayed it does nothing; as a target it unmakes; as a source it conjures.
The word for water.
Loose grains. The cheapest matter there is.
Soil.
Rock.
Timber. Burns.
Flame. Sprayed it ignites what it lands on.
Blood. The cheapest thing a body can be mended with.
Meat.
Bone.
Eats stone and meat alike.
Molten stone.
Does not burn, does not dissolve. Dear.
The dearest common matter. Making it is what kills alchemists.

The wildcard. Matches whatever is actually there. DANGEROUS: it is priced as the matter it turns out to be, plus a surcharge, and billed when it resolves - you do not know the price until it lands. The surcharge is a knob (anythingSurchargeMille, +50% to start).
An explosion at the point. Power adds with repetition; radius follows the engine law; priced by volume.

wind.comment: kind: cone (a jet) | burst (radial push, or a vacuum at negative speed) | vortex (swirl about the axis, with swirl/rise as the tangential and axial shares). speed is m/s. radius and reach are world cells. ticks is the hard lifetime bound (rule 2). entrain grants the licence to pull SETTLED powder loose inside the footprint, which is what spends the per-tick chunk wake budget.

glyphs.desc: A wind jet from the point along the aim. Repetition doubles speed, not size.
A vacuum burst: pulls loose matter and bodies toward the point. (Replaced on the page by `wind`, which says the same thing as a number; kept so old pages still work.)
One spark: an electric crackle that lives a tick or two. Pops hydrogen, splits molten salt, and only sometimes lights what burns beside it. The cheapest electricity there is.

strike.comment: No bolt: a burst of jagged arc walks out of the point (game/lightning.h, the storm's own strike function with height 0). Arc is tag:electric and lights what burns at a quarter chance a touch.

glyphs.desc: A crackle of arcs where it lands: short jagged discharges that run over what is there. Every electric reaction fires off it, and it sets dry things alight more readily than a spark.

strike.comment: A bolt from 40 cells above the struck top, which is the TALLEST thing within 5 cells of the point, a conductor (iron, copper, water) counting 6 cells taller than it is. Same function a storm's ground strike uses. Repetition raises the bolt and adds arcs.

glyphs.desc: Calls a bolt of lightning down on the point - or on the tallest conductor near it: a lightning rod draws it. Whatever burns where it lands goes up.
A transmute B: turns A into B where it resolves. Needs BOTH words; an empty side fizzles (charged).
M mend: draws matter M from the resolve point into the caster's missing anatomy cells, one voxel at a time. Needs a source word.
E trail: runs E at every marked voxel of the flight path. Needs a left word (matter is sprayed).

E aura: SUSTAINS E (or a mod) on the body at the resolve point - or on the place, if no body is there. Runs every tick, billed per tick to the caster and reserved out of their max mana, until the caster drops it or runs dry. `aura self` is a ward on yourself; `aura projectile` puts the same thing on whoever the bolt hits.
W null: a filter that refuses incoming ops of W's kind within the radius. Takes the word before it raw.
E echo: E repeats at the point every few ticks for a bounded span.
A bolt from the hand. Medium speed, resolves on impact.
Fast and light: twice the speed, half the kinetic impact.
Slow, arcing, heavy. Resolves on impact.
Slow, weightless, lingers; resolves on impact or when its life runs out.
A dropped rigid body with a fuse. Resolves where it comes to rest when the fuse runs out. The cheapest carrier.
Held: resolves at the ray hit every tick, billed per tick.
At the caster. From the character screen, at the chosen body part.
Splits into three, fanned. Said again in the same place it does nothing - to get nine, split each of the three branches. Everything behind it is paid for every bolt.
Anti-gravity. Twice: gravity reversed. On a body-anchored delivery it lifts the body. (Replaced on the page by `lift`, which says the same thing as a number; kept so old pages still work.)
Falls harder, hits harder. (Replaced on the page by `lift`, which says the same thing as a number; kept so old pages still work.)
Faster. (Replaced on the page by `speed`, which says the same thing as a number; kept so old pages still work.)
Slower. A slow explosive bolt is a mine that drifts. (Replaced on the page by `speed`, which says the same thing as a number; kept so old pages still work.)
Lives longer, reaches further; a bomb's fuse is longer.
Everything resolves over a wider radius. Priced by volume, so x8 per word.
Reflects off what it hits once more before resolving.
Passes through one body or thin wall before resolving.
Turns toward the nearest body.
Waits after impact before resolving; on a bomb, a longer fuse.

glyphs.example: explosive lane fire end twin projectile
glyphs.desc: Opens a LANE: a scope of the pile that belongs to ONE instance of the box that closes it. `end` closes it again. The first lane you open is what instance 0 carries on top of the shared items, the second what instance 1 carries, and so on; the box fires max(count, lanes) instances and an instance past the last lane carries the shared items alone. A delivery spoken INSIDE an open lane boxes only that lane, and the lane stays open — which is how a socket holds a bolt that fires a bolt. A lane is a wall: an operator cannot take a word from another scope, and identical words in different lanes do not merge. A mod inside a lane edits that instance's record - a `count` among them splits that one branch. With no delivery outside the lanes they are the hand's, which is how two unrelated spells are said at once: `lane explosive projectile end lane blood mend self end`.

glyphs.example: lane explosive projectile end lane fire end projectile
glyphs.desc: Closes the innermost open `lane`, back to the scope around it. A lane left open when the sentence runs out is closed for you; an `end` with nothing open is charged and does nothing.

glyphs.example: explosive lane fire end twin projectile
glyphs.desc: Splits into two, fanned. The double of `shotgun`'s triple, and like it one split per scope - said twice in one place the second is charged and does nothing. Everything behind it is paid for every bolt.

glyphs.axis: lift in g: +1 weightless, +2 rises, -1 falls twice as hard
glyphs.desc: How much gravity to take away, in g. 1 is weightless, 0.5 a slow fall, 2 rises; below zero it presses down instead. On a body-anchored delivery it lifts the body.

glyphs.axis: speed multiplier: x0.25 crawls, x4 flies
glyphs.desc: How fast it flies, as a multiple of its carrier's own speed. Below 1 it slows.

glyphs.axis: strength: positive blows out from the point, negative pulls in
glyphs.desc: A burst of wind at the point. Positive pushes loose matter and bodies away; negative is a vacuum that pulls them in.

summon.comment: A DEMON'S NAME IS A GLYPH (docs/PLAN_demons.md D1): the demon is assets/demons/<demon>.json, called up where the spell resolves. Into an intact salt circle it arrives CONTAINED; anywhere else it arrives loose and comes for you. Never granted by the debug default (SANDVOX_ALL_NAMES=1 grants every name); learned from a book. Keep the id: D2's smithy book grants it by this name.

glyphs.axis: nothing: a name said twice is one imp
glyphs.desc: The name of the imp Skerrick. Cast it into a closed ring of salt, from outside the ring, and he arrives held inside it. Cast it anywhere else and he arrives loose, and he remembers who called.

conjoined.comment: The grimoire's authored starter pages (plan section 12b): a saved list of glyph names that speaks exactly as if you had spoken them in order. Granted like glyphs, shown read-only; duplicate to your own grimoire to edit.

entries.desc: Draws blood within reach into your missing flesh. The starter mend: it can only draw on blood.
A bolt that leaves a burning wake.
A sustained field on yourself that refuses incoming transmute ops. Acid already flowing still flows.
A sand bolt that lands and then blows the landing flat.
Turns whatever it strikes into acid, priced by what it turns out to hit.
